tom_sales: Quick heads-up: Customer (FinEdge) wants to run a week-long POC. They want Redwood Private reachable from their VPC via PrivateLink or Transit GW + peering. Main asks: preserve source IPs to their backends, do split-DNS so internal hostnames resolve to endpoint IPs, and get a clear egress billing estimate. Can SE/NetOps confirm recommended pattern and a minimal firewall/SNAT snippet to include in the security questionnaire?

nina_se: Short take: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is safest for cross-account access and avoids route table overrides. Transit GW + peering works if they need full L3 reachability, but it's more invasive. For source IP retention: PrivateLink terminates at the ENI on our side, so customer-side proxy/NAT must preserve original client IP if they need it on their app logs.

kevin_net: For Transit GW option: you can keep src IPs if traffic flows directly (no SNAT on our side), but peering/transit path exposes broader routing. For PrivateLink, typical pattern: on-prem -> NAT or proxy w/ preserved src -> PrivateLink interface endpoint -> Redwood endpoint. DNS: we recommend split-horizon where `*.redwood.local` resolves to the endpoint's private DNS. Some customers use Route 53 private hosted zone or on-prem DNS override.

anna_sec: Security checklist items to attach to their questionnaire: 1) Minimal SG/ACLs (only allow customer's proxy subnet to our endpoint SG on 443), 2) TLS with server certs; optionally mTLS for mutual auth, 3) KMS key usage for customer-side encryption if they request BYOK, 4) retention window for flow logs and audit trails, 5) statement about IP stability and change windows.

tom_sales: They also want to know: If we route control plane telemetry over PrivateLink vs public egress, what extra ports or DNS names they need to allow?

nina_se: If they opt to route control plane over the same PrivateLink endpoint (agentless control-plane tunneling), no public egress is needed for control messages. If they prefer agent heartbeat to our public control plane, allow outbound 443 to `control.redwood-inference.com` and `metrics.redwood-inference.com`. We'll provide exact FQDNs.

kevin_net: Firewall sample (customer side): `# Allow proxy to Redwood endpoint`
`iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 10.10.20.0/24 -o eth0 -j SNAT --to-source 198.51.100.10`
`# Security Group (interface endpoint)`
`Inbound: TCP 443 from 10.10.20.0/24`
`Outbound: TCP 443 to 10.10.20.0/24`
Use vendor NAT mapping if they want a whole range translated.

anna_sec: Add sample ACL snippet for on-prem firewall: `permit tcp 10.10.20.0/24 host 198.51.100.10 eq 443` and mention that if they do TLS intercept, they must provide SNI or use mTLS to avoid breaking authentication.

kevin_net: DNS note: PrivateLink gives you option to enable private DNS so `api.redwood-inference.company` resolves inside VPC to the endpoint ENI IPs. If they use split-DNS, ensure DHCP options / resolvers point to your on-prem DNS that has the override. For Transit GW, standard VPC DNS applies.

tom_sales: Pricing: they asked if connector bandwidth (traffic over PrivateLink) is billed separately. Also curious about egress data transfer on our side vs their cloud egress.

nina_se: Short answer: POC: we can do a capped bandwidth allowance for the trial (no extra charge up to X TB). Production: pricing depends on plan. The customer's cloud provider may bill them for data going through PrivateLink / NAT. Redwood bills for usage of hosted inference (tokens) and for Dedicated/Private we include reserved GPU hours; network egress from our infra to customer (if any) and third-party transit may be an additional line item in enterprise deals. I'll put an explicit note in the SE handoff.

anna_sec: Also include in questionnaire: whether they require us to terminate TLS or do end-to-end. If E2E required, we must support SNI preservation by the proxy. Note: DPI (TLS inspection) is not supported unless customer uses a proxy that re-establishes TLS and we accept that cert chain (mTLS recommended).

kevin_net: Tests for POC: 1) Create interface endpoint with SG allowing proxy subnet. 2) Configure split DNS to resolve `api.redwood-inference` -> endpoint IP. 3) From behind proxy run `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer poc-key" https://api.redwood-inference/v1/health` (expect 200). 4) Verify headers: `X-Forwarded-For` if proxy adds it, and/or app logs show client IP. 5) Simulate TLS intercept to validate SNI/mTLS behaviour.

tom_sales: Can someone assemble a tiny handoff pack (one page): recommended topology diagram (PrivateLink vs TransitGW), SG/iptables snippets, DNS tips, and the POC bandwidth cap wording? I want to send before EOD.

kevin_net: I'll assemble the topology ascii and exact ip ranges per region.

anna_sec: I'll draft the questionnaire answer bullets and the statement on IP stability: we guarantee stable ENI CIDR blocks per deployment; changes require 30 days notice and will be coordinated with the customer.

deploy-bot: Created POC ticket POC-4998 and attached checklist. Assigning to kevin_net and nina_se. :package:

tom_sales: Perfect — thanks all. If you can drop the mini-pack into the ticket Ill share with FinEdge legal and netops. :rocket:
